newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after CPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher on Wednesday, aided by a lower-than-expected report on the June Consumer Price Index, analysts said. The following are there comments:
PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION:
-- "This is better than expected...This again indicates that inflation at the retail level is not a concern."
-- "This provides confirmation that the Fed in all likelihood does not need to get off the sidelines, certainly at the August meeting and probably not at the September meeting."

-- "The equity market will probably go up and dance around (Dow) 8000 at the same time the long bond dances around the 6.50 (percent yield). So you've got a dual technical resistance shaping up here, that if the bond breaks through I think equities will as well."
The Labor Department reported the June CPI rose 0.1 percent compared to 0.1-percent rise in May.

The core CPI, excluding volatile food and energy components, was up 0.1 percent compared to a 0.2-percent rise in May. Economists in a Reuters poll had expected, on average, the overall and core June CPI to rise 0.2 percent in June.
PIERRE ELLIS, SENIOR ECONOMIST, PRIMARK DECISION ECONOMICS:

"This was a very good CPI. The core rate slowed down a bit...This had been an area of considerable risk, given the fact that wages have firmed. But this is not being passed through. Goods prices have been feeble, and are down in total in June."
-- "This is a very good situation, continuing the good news we have had for a long time and giving markets more room to advance."
ALAN ACKERMAN, MARKET STRATEGIST, FAHNESTOCK AND CO:

-- "The CPI was a pleasant surprise. We are likely to have a bullish bond market. The overall trend is up and the focus in on earnings expansion. It looks like Dow 8,000 is another record which will fall by the wayside shortly. Stocks are likely to open higher."
The 30-year Treasury bond was up 8/32 to yield 6.53 percent. The S&P 500 future rose 3.95 to 935.70.
